en.title: Damian McCarthy's 'Hokum' Drops on Hulu Just in Time for Halloween
en.summary: Get ready for a chilling Halloween season as director Damian McCarthy's latest folk horror, 'Hokum,' arrives on Hulu. The film stars Adam Scott as a writer grappling with grief and inspiration in the Irish countryside.
en.body:
Prepare yourselves, horror aficionados, because **Damian McCarthy**'s unsettling new film, **Hokum**, has officially landed on Hulu just in time to add a dose of dread to your Halloween marathon. For those who missed its theatrical run or are eager for a rewatch, this is the perfect opportunity to experience McCarthy's unique brand of Irish folk horror.

**Hokum** follows the journey of Ohm Bauman, a grumpy novelist played by **Adam Scott**, who travels to a remote Irish inn. Ostensibly there to scatter his parents' ashes, Bauman finds himself entangled in something far more sinister and ancient than he could have imagined. This isn't just another haunted hotel story; it's a descent into primal fears, woven with elements of Irish folklore. McCarthy, known for his critically acclaimed **Oddity** and **Caveat**, continues to explore the uncanny and the deeply unsettling, drawing audiences into worlds where the monstrous might not be what it seems.

As Leah Schnelbach of Reactor Mag aptly put it, “Sometimes monsters just ARE. Sometimes things that seem like monsters to our human eyes are actually beautiful. Maybe the supernatural elements are ‘real’ and maybe they aren’t—it doesn’t matter when the story’s good enough. And that’s what **Hokum** is doing.” The film promises a narrative that prioritizes atmosphere and psychological unease over jump scares, featuring a cast that includes **Peter Coonan**, **David Wilmot**, **Florence Ordesh**, **Will O’Connell**, and **Michael Patric**, alongside the aforementioned dead goat.

## A Chilling Tale for Avid Readers

McCarthy's work often resonates with a literary sensibility, delving into the psychological landscapes of his characters and the folklore that shapes their environments. **Hokum** appears to be no exception, offering a rich narrative tapestry for those who appreciate storytelling that lingers long after the credits roll. The presence of **Adam Scott**, known for his nuanced performances in projects like **Severance**, suggests a compelling character study at the heart of the horror. Fans of genre-bending narratives and atmospheric dread will find much to dissect and discuss within **Hokum**'s unsettling embrace, making it a must-watch for anyone seeking more than just surface-level scares.

## Streaming for the Season

For those eager to get their hands on this new horror offering, **Hokum** is now available to stream on **Hulu**. The film's arrival on the platform ensures that it will be accessible throughout the Halloween season, allowing new audiences to discover McCarthy's chilling vision and for dedicated fans to revisit its unsettling depths. Keep an eye out for further discussions and analyses of **Hokum**'s place within the modern folk horror landscape.
